notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022, from the Annual Financial Information Report the county files with the Local Government Commission, as published by the Census Bureau. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.

Includes the public school system, which the county funds and the Census counts as part of the county, shown as schools and left out of the services and overhead shares, as in Connecticut, Massachusetts and Virginia.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities and ABC liquor stores. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($8,288,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts contributions from PACs, unions and other organizations to candidates for county commissioner, sheriff, register of deeds and the county school board, filed with the State Board of Elections since 2023. North Carolina bans corporate contributions. Individuals and party and candidate committees are not counted. Committees are placed by office and filing address, so a few may be assigned to a neighbouring county.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-14. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for North Carolina yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: The Forsyth County Sheriff’s Office uses automated license plate readers, according to a November 2022 Winstom-Salem Journal report.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS002048, citing Winston Salem Journal

redFlags.label: Real-time crime center
redFlags.detail: The Forsyth County Sheriff's Office utilizes the Fusus real-time crime center platform.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS011284, citing Fusus
